newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Soyuz with relief crew docks with Mir.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Soyuz with relief crew docks with Mir.

text.p: A Soyuz spacecraft with a two-man Russian relief crew docked on Thursday with the crippled Mir space station, Mission Control said. There was no sign of problems.
A wave of applause burst out and a huge sign "Congratulations" appeared on the screen of Mission Control outside Moscow. The docking took place one minute ahead of schedule, at 1702 GMT.

Commander Anatoly Solovyov, 49, and 43-year-old flight engineer Pavel Vinogradov are scheduled to meet the current three-men crew at about 1830 GMT when the hatch between Mir and Soyuz will be opened. The new crew face a daunting task of trying to restore power to the ageing station.

Mir suffered its worst accident on June 25, when a supply ship pierced its Spektr scientific module during a manual docking manoeuvre. Cosmonauts had to unplug power cables leading from Spektr's solar panels as they fled the module and sealed it. The accident deprived Mir of up to half of its power supply.

The two Russians, including commander Vasily Tsibliyev who has developed a stress-imposed heart problem, are scheduled to return to Earth on August 14. British-American physicist Michael Foale will remain on board until late September.
